message.content:
**Yes—you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta.** Noise violations are handled by the City of Atlanta’s **Code Enforcement** and **Police Department**. Here’s how you can do it: | Method | Details | |--------|---------| | **Online** | Use the City’s 311 portal: .
Navigate to “Noise” or “Public Safety” → “File a Complaint.” | | **Phone** | Call the 311 non‑emergency line: **404‑656‑4000**.
Ask to speak with the Noise Complaint Unit. | | **In‑person** | Visit City Hall: 100 Peachtree Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30303.
Go to the Office of Code Enforcement. | | **Email** | Send a detailed description to 311@atlantaga.gov. | ### What to Include - **Location** of the noise source (address or intersection). - **Time** and **duration** of the disturbance. - **Type of noise** (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). - **Any prior attempts** to resolve the issue (e.g., talking to neighbors). ### Legal Basis Atlanta’s municipal code (Title 10, Chapter 10.1) sets noise limits and defines when noise becomes unlawful. Violations can result in fines or other penalties. ### Follow‑up After filing, the city will assign a case number. You’ll receive updates via the 311 system or by phone/email. If the issue persists, you may request a follow‑up inspection. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on the specific noise ordinance or help drafting your complaint!
